claim: bandit B310 (x8) and semgrep dynamic-urllib-use-detected (x8): urllib.urlopen called with a dynamic value may permit file:// or a custom scheme.
rationale: All eight sites build the URL by concatenating onto a hardcoded scheme+host constant, so no caller can influence the scheme. results.py:53 uses API = "https://www.nationallottery.co.za/api" + a literal path from two in-module callers. backfill.py:57,136 use BASE (https, module constant) + a slug from the fixed PAYOUT_SLUG/ARCHIVE_SLUG dicts + an int year/date. supervise.py:473,518,529 use self.url, which supervise.py builds as "http://127.0.0.1:<port>" from an int port. tools/verify_page.py:410,1090 are the same localhost URL in a verifier. No untrusted input reaches any scheme, so the file:// vector the rule names is unreachable.

claim: bandit B608 tools/verify_watch.py:91: possible SQL injection through string-based query construction.
rationale: The f-string interpolates WHERE, the adb SQL WHERE clause the project imports as a constant, into a query over an in-memory sqlite3 database populated from the hardcoded BODIES fixture list at tools/verify_watch.py:60-83. Injecting that clause verbatim IS the check: INV-32 asserts that adb's WHERE clause and watch_sms.wanted() accept the same set, and parameterising it would remove the very string under test. No untrusted input, no persistent database, no network. The db is sqlite3.connect(":memory:") created three lines above.

results.py: the retry loop's only normal exit is the break after payload is assigned; HTTPError re-raises, and the URLError arm raises on the last attempt. Unbinding needs ATTEMPTS == 0, and results.py:29 already documents that exact condition inline ("ATTEMPTS = 3  # >= 1; at 0 the loop body never runs and `payload` is unbound"). tools/verify_page.py: each save and its restore sit under the identical broken("<name>") predicate - verified pairwise at 741/768 clear_model_on_failure, 1716/1745 found_on_first_build, 1750/1772 null_found_reads_as_zero, 1790/1827 summary_names_a_ticket, 1841/1925 no_drawn_numbers, 1850/1927 blank_numbers_cell. broken(name) is `return BREAK == name` against a module global set once from argv, so both sides always agree within one run; pyright cannot prove the predicate is stable.

claim: pyright reportOptionalOperand supervise.py:98,101: Operator "+" not supported for "None" on `line`.
rationale: `line = REFRESH_MESSAGE.get(outcome, outcome)` at supervise.py:91. Lines 98 and 101 are reachable only past `if outcome != REFRESH_DONE: return line` at 92, so at both sites outcome == REFRESH_DONE, which is a key of REFRESH_MESSAGE (supervise.py:52-65), so .get returns that key's str value and never the fallback. pyright does not correlate the narrowing of `outcome` at line 92 back to the type of `line` computed at line 91. Confirmed the None can't arrive from a caller either: the only production caller is tray.py:273, guarded by `if ok`, and Supervisor.refresh() (supervise.py:532-583) returns one of the four outcome strings on every path or raises - there is no implicit None return.

claim: pyright, remaining 21 diagnostics: reportOptionalMemberAccess (x9), reportFunctionMemberAccess (x5), reportOperatorIssue (x4), reportArgumentType serve.py:528 (x2) and tickets.py:161, reportCallIssue verify_page.py:1817, reportAttributeAccessIssue watch_sms.py:425.
rationale: serve.py:528 `int(raw)` where raw is headers.get("Content-Length") is wrapped in `except (TypeError, ValueError): return None, 400` - TypeError IS the None case, handled deliberately. tickets.py:161 MONTHS.index(m.group(2)) is LiteralString pedantry; .index accepts any str at runtime. watch_sms.py:425 `from gi.repository import GLib` - verified importable on this machine (GLib-2.0.typelib); gi is a dynamic introspection module with no stubs, so pyright cannot see it. tray.py:76 sup.child.wait() follows sup.start() on line 70 which assigns self.child; tray.py:311 QApplication.instance() inside a Qt slot cannot be None. The verify_page.py cluster is monkeypatch attribute assignment on function objects and .group() on a re.search whose pattern is asserted to match by the surrounding need() - and a verifier that did crash still exits non-zero, so it fails safe.

claim: vulture serve.py:487,491,492,494,572,612: unused variable 'protocol_version', 'server_version', 'sys_version'; unused method 'log_message', 'do_GET', 'do_POST' (all 60% confidence).
rationale: All six are BaseHTTPRequestHandler contract members on the Handler subclass at serve.py:486. protocol_version, server_version and sys_version are read by http.server when composing the status line and Server header - serve.py:488-492 documents that server_version/sys_version are set precisely to stop the default leaking an interpreter version. log_message is called by BaseHTTPRequestHandler.log_request; do_GET and do_POST are dispatched by BaseHTTPRequestHandler.handle_one_request from the request method name. None is referenced by project code by design, which is what vulture measures.

claim: typos: "VAS"/"vas" flagged 112 times across 21 files, and "empted" -> "emptied" at ROADMAP.md:1223.
rationale: VAS is the bank's own reference prefix for a Value Added Service transaction - it is the join key this project reconciles payouts on (check.py::reconcile), the documented privacy sentinel is literally VAS00000000000, and watch_sms.py::INCLUDE matches on the "vas00" prefix. It is a domain identifier, not an English word, and every one of the 112 hits is that identifier. ROADMAP.md:1223 reads "pre-empted", which is the correct spelling; typos' suggestion "emptied" is wrong for that context.

claim: yamllint .github/workflows/ci.yml:12:1: truthy value should be one of [false, true] - fires on the `on:` key.
rationale: `on` is the mandatory GitHub Actions trigger key. yamllint's truthy rule flags it because YAML 1.1 reads a bare `on` as boolean true, but quoting it or renaming it would break the workflow, which GitHub parses as YAML 1.2 where `on` is a plain string. The finding cannot be acted on without breaking the file it is about; the remedy would be a yamllint config setting truthy.check-keys false, which is a lint-contract decision rather than a code defect. CI has been green on this file across five runs (latest 2026-08-31).

claim: vulture serve.py:521,523,604 unused attribute 'close_connection'; serve.py:675,678,681,684,687 unused method 'do_HEAD','do_PUT','do_DELETE','do_OPTIONS','do_PATCH'.
rationale:
Added 2026-09-01 by the review-code fix pass, and both are the classes already recorded for do_GET/do_POST. The five new do_* methods are dispatched by BaseHTTPRequestHandler.handle_one_request from the request method name, exactly as do_GET and do_POST are; they exist so every method routes through _route()'s Host/path/method ladder instead of the stdlib's headerless 501. close_connection is a BaseHTTPRequestHandler attribute that handle() reads to decide whether to loop; this code only ever writes it, which is all vulture can see. Verified live: HEAD/PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS/PATCH each return 405 with the security headers and a bad Host still draws 421, and a POST whose body is not read closes the socket after one response.</rationale>
